evidence: Almost two thirds of surveyed tourist day visitors were from the Netherlands: 24% MRA and 41% elsewhere in the Netherlands. Domestic day visitors skew more toward shops and museums than foreign day visitors.

More than 7.5 million German overnight visitors to the Netherlands, about 35% of international staying visitors; city trips are among the top three holiday types and North Holland remains a major destination.
Belgian visitors represented 12% of the 21.3 million international visitors to the Netherlands in 2024; city-trip interest reached 28% and North Holland remains a major destination.

UK was the third-largest inbound market in NBTC Key Insights baseline; more than one third of non-business Netherlands trips are city trips. NBTC 2024 forecast estimated about 1.898 million UK staying visitors.
NBTC 2024 forecast estimated about 1.494 million US staying visitors; Americans show high advance booking behaviour, with 71% arranging attraction tickets before arrival in the inbound-visitor study.

France generated about 971,000 Netherlands visitors in 2023 and NBTC forecast roughly 1.013 million in 2024. Most stay in North Holland, mainly Amsterdam; 75% of French staying visitors in the inbound study visited Amsterdam.
Amsterdam recorded about 10 million staying visitors and 14 million tourist day visitors. Foreign day visitors commonly combine walking, museums, canals and multiple activities.
The Netherlands received 21.3 million international guests in 2024; North Holland and South Holland received the largest visitor volumes.
